Kādomon is a great blend of monster catchers, roguelites, and auto battlers. Fun team building with the Kādomon. Good run to run variance with the different items, field effects, and more. It even has something for shiny hunters - or in Kādomon, Misprints! Overall I highly recommend. It brings a really cool niche to the monster catcher genre.

I've managed to complete the first region in the prologue and I already need more. The auto battler system is intuitive and easy to pick up and synergize with. The Kadomon have fun little names and the art style for the game is cute and crisp. To help you get more in depth with your synergy and how to progress forward the game has a weakness/strengths chart that highlights the rows the cursor is currently hovering over making the information easier to see. Will likely play the demo some more to help scratch that autobattler itch but looking forward to the full release!

First autobattler I've tried after seeing the odd stream of them. Was a lot going on at first but with a bit more time got to understand better what was going up and make some cool teams with all the possible type combos, effects and items. And then was fun to try get all the final forms so looking forward to the next release!

It's also the slowest auto battler ever. Even on 3x speed rounds take forever. Current suggestion is no. If it gets fixed, it's quite possibly a yes.

I've played this game for a decent amount of time and... its got a long way to go. In terms of balance it isn't that great, every time I have won its been using the same team, not because I go for it but just because its the best. On my second run I found a shiny Scorpet which led me to believe shinies were common (they are not) and honestly this was awesome. But once I died due to not knowing the game well and found out that finding a shiny doesm't do anything, even in the kadodex. I would also go multiple runs seeing the same kadomon and then randomly a new one would appear. Yeah idk.

Lots of fun with many different play styles. i hope to see more kadomon in the future and hopefully this game will receive updates to keep the community engaged in a game that mixes lots of neat and loved ideas. definitely recommend.

Great game with an aesthetic reminiscent of Super Auto Pets, yet they are able to make this style their own with the inclusion of evolution. Gameplay is solid with my only gripe being that, depending on the speed you set the game too, battles either feel like they take too long because of all the effects my monsters are activating each and every turn or the battles feel too quick to understand what my monsters are actually doing. Despite this problem, I am eager for the full release of the game and will definitely keep an eye for future updates.

I think the concept of this game is amazing. But after playing the game for about 20 hours here are my critiques that I hope they fix for the full version: 1.) Difficulty Slider: This game is very easy A.T.M. I have beaten the game very easily only using 3/4 slots and with have just beaten the game with 2/4 slots used. Adding a difficulty progression like how ascension in slay the spire could help with this. 2.) Longer Run: based on context clues (I am guessing). Each run will one be one region long. But I feel like it is a too short. The game feels most enjoyable in the mid-late game once when get items, field effects, and good typings. But the game quickly ends and you have to start a new run. In the majority of runs you will only get 1-2 kadomon to max level. I imagine myself enjoying the game much more if could have develop a full team with a couple extra in reserve, swapping them in and out to respond to differences in the enemy composition. Making an endless mode or having the runs be 2-3 regions per run could be exciting. 3.) Adding a Puzzle mode: I think alternate mode that is level based/find the correct solution could be entertaining way to play the game. 4.) Way more diversity and in mystery events and mini boss rewards. Feels kinda bland and not worth it to go to the mystery events. The mini bosses could give you unique items or field effects when defeated. Having unique augments that effect how runs play out is a must in a game like this. Overall I enjoy the game a lot (I wouldn't have played the game for 20 hours if I didn't). But I hope they delay the full version to add new features, modes, and diversity to the game. I want this game to release as a S tier game. But I think currently it is a B.

Overwhelming at a glance, but just worry about the monsters in your party and you'll be fine. The rest you'll learn in time. Played three runs and found some pretty powerful synergies quite reliably, and of different types too. - One of them was focused on a support mon activating the super of the guy in front three times at the start of the battle and setting up instantly. - Another was a group of fighting type mons that unlocked the type-specific bonus of attacking enemies get hit with a defense defuff, and capitalising on that with a mon with innate multi-hit. - The third was a group of monsters with quick-charging supers and one monster whose passive inflicted poison every time a super went off paired with another monster in the front who gained block any time poison was applied. The monster designs are super cute/cool too. Looking forward to [strike]the "fanart"[/strike] more designs coming in the full release!

"Kādomon: Hyper Auto Battlers Prologue" is is not a game. It's an advertisement for a product called "Kādomon: Hyper Auto Battlers". Kādomon: Hyper Auto Battlers is essentially a mobile app in exile, a "card" and monster battler, a Pokemon themed ripoff of Slay the Spire. Which is not to say it doesn't have any value or depth if you think your gaming rig is best used to play iPhone games, but it's hard to recommend that kind of thing to cutting edge PC gamers. But this isn't completely relevant because this is not Kādomon: Hyper Auto Battlers, it's just an advertisment for it, so it's not correct to try to review that completely distinct product. We must instead review this for what it is... an advertisement. If you enjoy advertisements, you can consume them for free on the web or on Youtube without needing to add them to your game library, download them, and then launch the advertising. It's impossible in a general sense to recommend people should do that over playing real, full games on Steam, and that applies here with "Kādomon: Hyper Auto Battlers Prologue" too. The purpose of this advertisement is to get you to shell out a whopping $10 USD on buying Kādomon: Hyper Auto Battlers, and I don't recommend you do that either. As an advertisement, this is only free in the same way that adverts on Youtube and banner ads in your browser are. This is a game demo that's been dumped on Steam to advertise another Steam store page in the hopes of raking in some cash. Just because advertisements are free, doesn't mean they're worth your time. It's important to understand there's a formal process to create a demo/page for a game which hasn't been followed here: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/application/demos While it might seem like an inocuous mistake, publishing demos and advertisements as if they are full games is misleading and in some ways harmful. This advertisement is taking up marketing space and visibility that would be better made available to a developer that's done the right thing and created a full game. Instead, that visibility is given over to a demo/advert that's been published incorrectly and is polluting the marketplace. It's unclear if this mistake was made through incompetence or a deliberate intent to mislead gamers. Often developers may choose to incorrectly publish demo/advertisements as separate games as a cheap way to bypass paying Valve for marketing presence on the Steam front page, which may seem clever to them, but it's harmful behaviour and it's not good for gamers. Advertisements and incorrectly published demos don't add +1 to your game collector count, they aren't full games. It's impossible for me to recommend this incorrectly published advertising spam to gamers, you deserve better than adverts.
